The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of S.R.Muniswamy, in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 27.1.2024 at about 11.30 a.m. S.R.Muniswamy was riding TVS XI Super two wheeler bearing No.KA-02-HC-6174, when he was going from T.B. Cross to Srinivasapura on the extreme left side in NH-44 road, which runs from Hyderabad to Bengaluru, beside Krishnareddy Pettige Shop, infront of Gangothri Petrol Pump,
Bagepalli Taluk, at that time the rider of two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50-EH-6813 came in opposite direction from H.P. Petrol pump, in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the deceased- Muniswamy.
As a result, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Bagepalli for treatment, then he was shifted to NIMHANS,
Bengaluru wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 15 days, surgery was conducted for his head injuries.
Thereafter, again doctor has advised to go to Government Hospital, Bagepalli for follow-up treatment.

Thereafter he was shifted to Government Hospital, Bagepalli and then District Hospital,
inspite of treatment he was succumbed to the injuries on 16.2.2024.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy, aged about 68 years and doing coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark,
causing lot of pain, shock and mental agony.
4. It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the riding of the rider of two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50- EH-6813.
In this regard, Bagepalli Police have registered the case against the rider of the Motor cycle in Crime No.46/2023 for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their written statement.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 has contended that the vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
Further contended that there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of two wheeler bearing registration NoKA-50-EH-6813 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the rider of offending vehicle.
It is also contention of the respondent that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.

Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive,
exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.S.R.Muniswamy died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 27.1.2024 at about 11.30 a.m. infront of Gangothri Petrol Pump, NH-44 Bagepalli Taluk, Chickballapura,
Karnataka, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of two wheeler bearing Nagaraju S M vs Murthy on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26449747/
3 registration No.KA-50- EH-6813 in an actionable negligence?
2)
Whether the petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, at what rate ? From whom?
4) What order or award?

10. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW1 & got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA- 50-EH-6813, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, S.R.Muniswamy died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

15. On the other hand, the respondents have contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50-EH-6813.
16.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the rider of the offending vehicle in question.
17. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name S.M.Nagaraju examined as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.46/2024 of Bagepalli Police Station.
Ex. P2-true copy of the first information statement given by S.M.Nagaraju,
Ex.P3-true copy of statement of complainant, Ex.P4- true copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P5-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P6- -true copy of IMV Report, Ex.P7- true copy of Inquest Report, Ex.P8-true copy of PM Report and Ex.P9-true copy of charge sheet.

18. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Nagaraju, the S.H.O. of Bagepalli Police have registered the case against the rider of two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50- EH-6813 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of I.P.C. & Section 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against rider of the motor cycle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC & Section 187 of IMV Act.
19.
In order to substantiate the defence of the respondents the respondent No.1 has examined as RW1.
He has deposed in his evidence that Muniswamy was died due to age factor and not due to the accident.

The petitioners with an intention to get money from the respondents colluding with the police have falsely implicated his vehicle, even the deceased was not in a position to ride his vehicle due to his old age factor.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that as per Ex.P1 & Ex.P2 case is filed against him.
Further admitted that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against him.
Further he had gone to the police station to give complaint, but police have not received his complaint, but he had no impediment to give the complaint to the higher authorities.
On going through the evidence of RW1 & his cross- examination, it is crystal clear that he has failed to establish the allegation made against him.

20. Apart from this, PW1 was subjected for cross-examination but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the Nagaraju S M vs Murthy on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26449747/
5 offending vehicle.
21.
In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50-EH-6813 and in the said accident, S.R.Muniswamy succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 and 3:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P14 i.e., Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
23. In the case on hand, no doubt the major sons and daughter of S.R.Muniswamy filed this claim petition.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during his lifetime.
In the cross-examination PW1 has stated that himself, petitioner No.2 & 3 were doing coolie.
At this stage, it is necessary discuss the point that, father place an important role in the family.

All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors,
married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

24. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their mother during her lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.
In this regard, the petitioner has relied the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (DB)
, in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application, irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

25. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are the sons of the deceased have lost their love and affection of the deceased, who was the backbone of the family.

Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
26. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhaar card, which is marked at Ex.P11 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the year of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1953.
The accident occurred on 27.1.2024.

Therefore,
as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 71 years.

For his age, multiplier '5' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
27.
In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2024.
By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- for the year 2024.
28 . Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
29.

Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
30. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are 3 persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.

sentences.text: In the present case, deceased was aged about 71 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "5" is applicable.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,98,000/- per year.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.1,98,000-Rs.66,000).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "5" which comes to Rs.6,60,000/-.
32.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

33. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.18,150/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.48,400/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

In this regard he has placed the medical bill at Ex.P10 for Rs.1,115/-.
There are are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bill.

LIABILITY:
37.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50-EH-6813, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
38. As per Ex.R2 insurance policy was valid from 11.5.20222 to 10.5.2027.
The alleged accident had taken place on 27.1.2024.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Hence,
respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative and issue No.3 is Partly Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
39.

In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,42,615/- (Rupees eight lakhs forty two thousand six hundred and fifteen only), together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for equal share.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 to 3, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.S.R.Muniswamy died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which took place on 27.1.2024 at about 11.30 a.m. infront of Gangothri Petrol Pump, NH-44 Bagepalli Taluk, Chickballapura,
Karnataka, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of two wheeler bearing Nagaraju S M vs Murthy on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26449747/
3 registration No.KA-50- EH-6813 in an actionable negligence?
2)
Whether the petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation? If so, at what rate ? From whom?
4) What order or award?

George Menezes I have gone through the supra decisions "the common principle laid down in the supra decision is that the major sons and married daughters are also dependents of the deceased person."
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against rider of the motor cycle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC & Section 187 of IMV Act.
19.
On going through the evidence of RW1 & his cross- examination, it is crystal clear that he has failed to establish the allegation made against him.
20. Apart from this, PW1 was subjected for cross-examination but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the Nagaraju S M vs Murthy on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26449747/
5 offending vehicle.
21.
Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-50-EH-6813 and in the said accident, S.R.Muniswamy succumbed to the injuries.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
24. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their mother during her lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"
Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The alleged accident had taken place on 27.1.2024.

ISSUE No.4:
39.
In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,42,615/- (Rupees eight lakhs forty two thousand six hundred and fifteen only), together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for equal share.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 to 3, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
